DIXON.name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
DIXON.grounding_note: Illustrative sample. In live mode, quotes come from the company's own concall transcripts and annual report; figures come from Screener.in's standardised tables, labelled as a secondary source and reconciled to results filings where available.

business_snapshot.what: India's largest electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company — designs and builds products for global and domestic brands (ODM/OEM).

segments.name: Mobile & EMS
segments.note: Smartphones + feature phones; the growth engine. Key anchor customers under PLI.

segments.name: Consumer Electronics (TVs)
segments.note: LED TVs for large brands; mature, lower-margin.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.note: LED bulbs/battens; the original business, now small.

segments.name: Others (Wearables, Telecom, Display)
segments.note: Display fab is the new optionality.

business_snapshot.model: Thin-margin, high-asset-turn. Value accrues via scale, backward integration (components, display) and ODM share gains.

trajectory.read: Revenue compounding ~10% QoQ for four quarters while margin grinds up ~30bps — operating leverage plus mix shift to ODM/display. The margin line is the thing to watch: EMS bulls are paying for the slope, not the level.

points.read: Modest; capex largely internally funded + PLI.
Negative-to-low WC is the EMS superpower — suppliers + advances fund growth.
Mostly customs/duty disputes; ~9% of net worth — monitor, not alarming.
Display fab + component backward-integration. The leverage risk lives here if ramp slips.

cash_quality.read: Cash conversion improving as scale normalises working capital. Still below 1.0 — profits are real but growth consumes cash, so FCF is thin while in capex phase. Not a red flag; a growth-stage signature.

bull: ODM + backward integration structurally lifts a 4% margin toward 5–6% over time — small bps moves are large on this base.
Display fab is a call option the market is only starting to price; pulled forward vs guidance.
Negative working capital means growth is self-funding — rare in a capex-heavy story.
bear: Still a ~4% EBITDA-margin assembler; customer concentration and pricing power are real constraints.
Valuation discounts years of flawless execution — any display-ramp slip re-rates it hard.
Capex intensity (₹1,900 cr) could pressure the clean balance sheet if volumes disappoint.

commitments.quote: We expect Q4 revenue to comfortably exceed 11,500 crore.
Margins should inch towards 4.3% by the exit of FY27.
We are confident of 40%-plus PAT growth in the first quarter.
The display JV should start contributing from H2 FY27; we are not baking in any revenue in H1.
commitments.note: qualitative milestone that needs segment disclosure; flagged for analyst review
commitments.label: Display JV contribution

commitments.quote: For FY27 we expect revenue to cross 55,000 crore.
We are guiding to an EBITDA margin band of 4.3 to 4.5% for the year.
With a full quarter of display, Q3 should see a further margin step-up.

DIXON.ledger_read: Every commitment that has reached its evaluation date was met or beaten. The larger FY27 calls are still open: H1 revenue annualises just under the ₹55,000 cr marker, while year-to-date margin sits inside the guided band.

ASIANPAINT.name: Asian Paints Ltd
ASIANPAINT.grounding_note: Illustrative sample. In live mode, quotes come from the company's own concall transcripts and annual report; figures come from Screener.in's standardised tables, labelled as a secondary source and reconciled to results filings where available.

business_snapshot.what: India's largest paints company; decorative paints dominate, with a growing home-décor and industrial (via JVs) adjacency.

segments.name: Decorative (India)
segments.note: Core; volume + mix driven. Under new competitive pressure.

business_snapshot.model: Brand + distribution moat (>150k dealers, tinting machines). Pricing power historically strong — now being tested.

trajectory.read: The classic 'narrative vs numbers' setup: a franchise with pristine returns whose margin line has fallen four quarters running as new entrants discount. The level (16%) is still good; the slope is the worry.

points.read: Fortress balance sheet — can out-spend competitors on A&P and capacity.
New capacity amid a demand-soft patch — defending share.

cash_quality.read: Cash conversion remains excellent (~0.93) even as margins slip — profits are high quality and real. The problem is the P&L, not the cash flow.

bull: Best-in-class returns and a net-cash balance sheet — it can simply outlast new entrants.
Cash conversion ~0.93 proves earnings quality is intact; this is a margin dip, not a business break.
If pricing normalises, the operating leverage snaps margin back fast off the current trough.
bear: Three consecutive guidance misses on margin — management's forward credibility is impaired.
Competitive intensity looks structural, not 'transient' as framed — a permanent re-rate of the moat.
Premium valuation still embeds pricing power that the numbers are actively questioning.

commitments.quote: We see fourth-quarter margins holding above 18.5%.
We remain comfortable with our 18 to 20% margin band for FY27.
Competitive intensity is transient; we expect Q1 margins back above 18%.
The festive quarter will be volume-led and we expect at least 5% revenue growth.
We expect margins to recover to around 17% by the exit of FY27.
We will return to double-digit volume growth.
commitments.note: volume growth is not disclosed in the standard financial tables
commitments.label: Volume growth

ASIANPAINT.ledger_read: All three commitments that have come due were missed, each on margin or growth recovery. The FY27 band and exit-margin calls remain open, but year-to-date margin is already below both.

INFY.name: Infosys Ltd
INFY.grounding_note: Illustrative sample. In live mode, quotes come from the company's own concall transcripts and annual report; figures come from Screener.in's standardised tables, labelled as a secondary source and reconciled to results filings where available.

business_snapshot.what: Global IT services and consulting; large-deal and digital/AI transformation led.
business_snapshot.model: People + platforms; margin is a function of utilisation, pricing and onsite mix. AI is both a tailwind (deals) and a deflation risk (pricing).

trajectory.read: Low-single-digit revenue grind with a steadily rising margin — a cost-discipline story more than a growth story right now. The guidance raise this quarter is what changes the read.

cash_quality.read: Textbook cash quality — FCF slightly exceeds PAT. Earnings are as real as it gets; the debate is growth, never accounting.

bull: Guidance raise signals genuine demand inflection, not just cost control.
Net-cash, >1.0 cash conversion, ≥85% FCF returned — a compounder's cash profile.
Margin discipline proven across a soft demand year.
bear: Still low-single-digit CC growth — AI-led pricing deflation is a real medium-term overhang.
FS concentration leaves it cyclically exposed.
Valuation prices a recovery that the guidance only just started to confirm.

commitments.quote: We expect Q4 operating margin to stay at or above 20%.
Our FY27 revenue growth guidance is 1 to 3% in constant currency.
commitments.note: constant-currency growth can't be derived from INR-reported figures (target shown in %)
commitments.label: Constant-currency revenue growth

commitments.quote: Operating margin guidance for FY27 is 20 to 22%.
We expect second-quarter revenue to grow at least 3% year on year.
We expect first-half profit growth of at least 5%.
We are raising FY27 constant-currency growth guidance to 3.5 to 4.5%.
commitments.note: constant-currency growth can't be derived from INR-reported figures (target shown in %)
commitments.label: Constant-currency revenue growth

INFY.ledger_read: Conservative targets, consistently met or beaten, and the FY27 operating-margin band is on track year to date. The constant-currency growth guidance (now raised) can't be checked from INR-reported tables, so it is shown unscored.
